definitions.explanation: Words of praise that may not be entirely sincere, often said to please someone or be polite.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}⟦でも→でも：00925_demo⟧⟦うれしい→嬉しい：00822_ureshii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: Even if it's just flattery, I'm happy to hear it.
I can't say it's good, even as a compliment.
examples.notes: Set phrase for 'not even being polite can make it good.'

notes:
お{世辞|せじ} is praise offered to please the listener rather than to report an honest opinion — the compliment that smooths a social occasion. Calling something お{世辞|せじ} implies it may not be sincere, so it is not normally used of one's own praise except to disclaim it.

Formation: お (polite prefix) + ⟦{世辞|せじ}→世辞：15102_seji⟧ 'compliment'. The bare ⟦{世辞|せじ}→世辞：15102_seji⟧ exists but is rarely used alone; the お form is the ordinary word.

Collocations:
- お{世辞|せじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧: to pay someone a compliment
- お{世辞|せじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧: good at flattery
- お{世辞|せじ}⟦{抜|ぬ}き→抜き：23505_nuki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧: frankly, flattery aside
- お{世辞|せじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧〜⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: can't call it ~ even generously — a fixed frame for polite understatement, as in example 3

Similar words:
- ⟦{褒|ほ}め{言葉|ことば}→褒め言葉：19432_homekotoba⟧: words of praise, with no implication of insincerity
- ⟦おべっか→おべっか：07885_obekka⟧: brown-nosing, sucking up — openly negative
- ⟦{追従|ついしょう}→追従：07883_tsuishou⟧: fawning, sycophancy (formal, strongly negative)
- ⟦{社交辞令|しゃこうじれい}→社交辞令：11081_shakoujirei⟧: social pleasantries — the wider category of things said for form's sake
